summary: ZENITH DNIPRO is an educational 3D space mission simulator. Players act as chief engineers, designing rockets by balancing mass, budget, fuel, and power to complete four progressive missions: launching satellites, conducting EVA repairs, docking with the ISS, and deploying constellations, making aerospace engineering accessible.
details:
Our project is an educational 3D space mission simulator where players act as the chief engineer of a growing space program. Players progress through four distinct missions—launching a scientific satellite, performing an EVA space repair, docking with the International Space Station (ISS), and deploying an orbital satellite constellation. Gameplay requires designing custom rockets from scratch by balancing mass, budget, fuel, engine power, energy consumption, and scientific payload. Once constructed, players can test and launch their spacecraft using automatic, assisted, or manual flight controls to complete specific scientific objectives.

The project bridges the gap between entertainment and education by making complex aerospace engineering and orbital mechanics accessible and engaging. Its intended impact is to inspire students and young space enthusiasts, fostering critical thinking, resource management, and a deeper practical understanding of physics and space exploration.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the project utilizes modern 3D game development tools, physics engines, and programming languages to simulate realistic orbital mechanics, rocket staging, and spacecraft telemetry.

Unlike traditional space games that either overly simplify flight physics or overwhelm users with unapproachable math, ZENITH uniquely integrates engineering constraints (such as strict budgets and component reliability) directly into a structured, narrative-driven campaign. Every design choice made on Earth directly impacts mission success in orbit, balancing realistic engineering physics with an intuitive user interface.
